Why does flesh rejoice, which is being prepared as food for worms?  
Now is the place for weeping, the time for atoning for sins.  
Later he will rejoice who now weeps for his crimes;  
Already he may rejoice, because he merits the highest joys.  
The joys of fools heap up increases of evils.  

[Col. 1308A] The prudent flee such things, despising them.  
Why do you not swiftly reject what you see passing away?  
Do you not see the world, utterly weak and dying,  
Perishing in languor beneath the sword of dreadful death?  

Death cuts down; behold, death kills whatever is created in flesh.  
It crushes the great and the small; it rules all.  
It holds sway alike over leaders and princes;  
It possesses the power of nobles and respects no one.  
Death snatches young and old alike, sparing none.  
It rages; every race that moves upon the earth trembles.  
It strikes; all flesh perishes. While beneath death’s foot  
The strong man is crushed, he is not rescued by his strength.  

Why then does one who dies thus wish to be magnified?  
Why does he desire immense riches to be amassed for himself?  
We are unstable and frail, and by many calamities  
[Col. 1308B] are worn down: thus already we are drawn toward the time of our end.  
All mortal things pass away and do not return.  
Nothing remains beyond a doubtful span; night and day  
Brief life, like a fleeting shadow, is thus reduced to nothing;  
It goes on and suddenly falls when it thinks itself standing.  

Who can ransom one while death destroys him? Who can make terms with it anywhere?  
Death never accepts either payment or servitude.  
But why say more? Wicked death spares no one:  
Neither the poor man escapes nor he who fills his purse.  

Therefore do not cease to do good things;  
For death does not cease to threaten you by night and day.  
Do not hope any longer in transient things;  
Rather, let your mind desire the joys of eternal light.  

The fool is deceived by love of the present life;  
But the wise man knows how full it is of pain.  
[Col. 1309A] Whatever beautiful and precious thing the world possesses  
Has the nature of a flower to which nature gives color;  
As soon as it withers, all its color is destroyed.  
Thereafter it shows no flower and breathes no fragrance.  

Royal majesty, every earthly power,  
The prosperity of possessions, a long succession of days,  
Will pass without delay when the hour of death comes.  
We do not know the hour of death; we know death well.  
Reputation does not know how to die; no honor is proof against death.  
Hear what honor is—but I do not endeavor to write it for you;  
For you know well enough that it has no usefulness.  

Landed estates, possession of riches,  
The building of walls, the grand construction of houses,  
The pleasures of tables with luxurious banquets,  
Distinguished beds, handsome cups and goblets,  
[Col. 1309B] glittering clothing that obstructs honorable conduct,  
Herds of cattle, the spacious cultivation of fields,  
A fruitful vineyard filled with diverse vines,  
The glory of children and sweet love for them—  
All will be left behind and will not be found hereafter.  

What wise person cares to seek that which lasts only briefly?  
Harsh death, fearing no man, will make an end  
Of lying and unhealthy worldly things.  

The grave cause of sins, love of women, will cease—  
Their conversation is nothing but bitter poison,  
Offering cups of gall beneath honey’s sweetness.  
For their beauty is a deceptive snare for souls;  
With flattering, deceitful, and wicked words  
It ensnares fools and brings many to Tartarus.  

Times will pass and vain joys perish,  
[Col. 1309C] and they will bear the sad fruit of weeping through the ages.  
I say this to all, that they may not subject themselves to the enemy;  
He who is caught and held in these things is overthrown.  

Do not be confounded by the wretched sweetness of the world;  
For its sweetness dissolves in a foul course.  
It deceives lukewarm minds and all who pursue softness,  
Caressing the flesh and gently indulging it.  

893 Thereafter it ends and is no longer found sweet.  
Instead it becomes exceedingly bitter, its end not equaling its beginning,  
And it grievously stings the wretches whom at first it anointed.  
For it tortures in fire after death those thus deceived  
And ever accustomed to pleasures, deservedly condemned;  
It turns pleasure into anguish,  
And becomes a raging flame burning them without end.  
Such gains will those reap who cling to such pursuits.  

[Col. 1309D] But he who wishes to be saved and blessed forever  
Should strive to give himself wholly in devotion to Christ.  
By clinging to his commands and doing  
What the teachings of the holy Scriptures show,  
He will truly receive the gifts of eternal rest in joyful dwellings—  
He who wishes to keep these commands,  
Which are given to all who serve God from the heart.  
This is the rest and life of his servants.  

No tribulation troubles the joys he grants;  
Solemn glory abides for them, and enduring peace.  
He always makes those whom he receives with himself  
Honored and blessed; and though he judges what is just,  
Yet more is given to the saints than they deserve.  
The fountain of divine mercy gives all things freely,  
[Col. 1310A] and in return for brief labor grants gifts of an everlasting age.  

Thus many rewards are prepared for those who are saved;  
Thus destructive death prepares many evils for the wicked.  
The former will rejoice; the latter will grieve without end.  
No one can tell, see, or conceive  
The joys of the righteous—or the torments of the wicked.  

How grievously deceived is he who foolishly makes sport,  
Who, for the flower and empty beauty of the world,  
Which first appears like dew and immediately dries up,  
Goes to hell, losing the heavenly crown  
Which the Lord gives to all whom he himself crowns!  

Truly the person errs who, though able to possess good things,  
Voluntarily undergoes punishments and infernal chains.  
Love of this world prepares the depths of the profound pit;  
He who is cast into it dies, immediately extinguished.  
[Col. 1310B] He always falls to the depths; death always goes to meet him;  
Venerable old age does not reach the bounds of death.  
Knowing no end, and seeming always to arise,  
Ever tormenting and ever renewing groans,  
It inflicts burning pains and infinite sufferings.  

There are serpents there vomiting flames from their mouths,  
Deformed and black, yet not slow to strike.  
They are never relaxed but ever renewed for these tasks;  
Fiercely burning, they are fresh for torment,  
Always sorrowful and always ready to strike;  
They always blaze, never cease, nor rest.  
Thus they exact punishment: they neither spare nor pity.  
How wretchedly condemned and how violently tortured  
Is he who bears the savagery of so many punishments!  

What will treasures or a heap of gold profit you  
[Col. 1310C] when sinners are sent to the lower  
Recesses of hell, to fire and likewise darkness,  
To suffer them forever and never return from them?  

He who is delivered to these punishments weeps and is sad;  
He would prefer to have lived poor throughout all his former life  
Rather than to have possessed riches.  
He stands poorly secure who is about to fall at once;  
Nor does he rightly rejoice for whom punishment and pain are prepared.  

Therefore do not seek to acquire greater treasures—  
Deceptive, uncertain, and fleeting treasures,  
Which are desired more eagerly when more fully accumulated  
And never satisfy minds always demanding more.  
Such riches are ruinous to all.  
For they make miserable and needy those who trust in them  
After the life of the flesh, nourished through flatteries;  
[Col. 1310D] deprived of good, they are delivered to perdition.  

Yet let no one believe that, if he keeps his own goods or heaps up riches,  
He must necessarily depart from this light to burn in fires or perish because of wealth.  
Although it is rare, their possessor can be saved justly  
If he avoids the name of miser.  
Let him live wisely and possess wealth wisely:  
Not by hiding it, but by distributing it to the needy.  

But it is well enough known that to leave everything behind  
894 profits more than rashly to hold uncertain things.  
It is truly safer to take care by fleeing a bite  
Than to lie down near serpents bearing poison.  

If you now feel horror of the world, I give you this counsel:  
Despise it, and with a joyful heart give yourself  
[Col. 1311A] to the service of Christ, to whom you yourself were entrusted.  
He will offer you a kingdom that has no end.  
If you give yourself to him, you will attain lofty riches  
Which thieves cannot take away nor mice gnaw.  

Gather a treasure surpassing gems and gold,  
One that stores up good inward habits for you.  
Integrity of mind surpasses heaped-up wealth.  
How miserable he is—and will be—who seeks the world’s prosperity!  
He is truly rich who does not care to possess such things.  

He who is good, guarded within by the defense of faith,  
Always keeps zeal for honor and uprightness.  
When anyone practices good, then he fits himself for virtues;  
If there is no filth to defile the depths of his heart,  
The Lord who searches the heart delights in him.  

[Col. 1311B] Such a precious spiritual treasure  
Obtains eternal life and the heavenly homeland.  
Every faithful person gathers treasures in heaven  
And through good habits reaches toward the highest honors.  
He neither wishes to become rich nor to be considered great,  
But always to be least, despised, and lowly,  
Desiring poverty more than prosperity.  
He endures these things because he hopes for heaven’s joys.  

The lovable and venerable poor person is blessed;  
The useless and wretched rich person is cursed.  
He who neglects good and loves evil enters the abyss.  
No power and no money frees him.  
In that miserable, insatiable gulf,  
Where he is submerged, every fearful image is seen.  

These torments were deserved by their sins  
[Col. 1311C] and undergone by the wretched man and grieving Eve.  
Had they kept God’s merciful and salutary commands,  
Neither man nor woman nor their offspring would have perished through death.  
But because they did not fear to break and despise his commands,  
Grievous death rushed in; this was deserved, and they perished.  

The gate of death, a mighty injury, their sin,  
Brought into the world the seeds of disease and so many evils.  
That fault destroyed the parents and their descendants  
And took away the gift of pious delights.  
A lamentable deed, bringing torment and pain,  
Made them deserve to lose the love of the true King,  
To perish under a lot so tearful and hateful,  
And to undergo the confines of savage punishments.  

Through Eve was given the cause of cruel destruction,  
[Col. 1311D] when she hoped for higher honors at the dragon’s voice.  
Believing it wickedly, and injuring us too by a great sin,  
Under this mournful omen she subjected the ages to ruin.  
Thereafter the stock of wretches, full of pains, increased;  
Subject to these evils, it wept through many years.  

Then God Almighty, who created all things by his word,  
Grieving that the man whom he had always loved had fallen thus,  
Sent his own Word to the lowest parts of the world  
To open ways of return for wretched exiles.  

Therefore the Son of God descended from the heavenly height,  
Never descending from the Father’s majesty.  
Taking a body endowed with life, while his divinity remained inviolate,  
He came forth, born from the womb of the holy Virgin.  

True man and true God, merciful and compassionate,  
[Col. 1312A] the true Savior and lover of our salvation,  
Wishing to show us the rule of life,  
He gave himself as an example and as the right pattern in all things.  
Moreover, he was willing to undergo many labors  
And by his own suffering to take away our sufferings.  
Dying of his own will, by dying he conquered death,  
And thus redeemed wretches from perpetual death.  

Paying what he did not owe, the fountain of mercy  
Came to the aid of us burdened by the deadly plague.  
Bearing our burdens, he wholly relieved us,  
And restored whatever ancient sin had taken away.  
For, rising mercifully from death like a strong lion,  
He restored life after overthrowing the prince of death.  
Thus the Lord’s mercy, not allowing the world to perish,  
895 made us wretches return to the first joys.  

[Col. 1312B] Brother, you have now heard sufficiently that Christ’s grace  
Saved us thus and renewed our race.  
If you are wise, you believe this and do not depart from this truth.  
But what does one gain by believing if he does not act?  
He badly harms himself; living badly, he does not believe rightly.  
Believe me: that faith does itself greater harm  
Than if it had not known what the doctrine of faith was.  
It gains death, and is rightly called dead.  
It makes its possessor die under a graver judgment.  

What I say is well known and wholly useful to those who keep it.  
Brother, hear it: many benefits will come to you  
If you wish to retain it, for thus you yourself will be faithful.  
Through this power you will be able to keep salvation,  
And you will be blessed if you do what is good.  

Therefore always remember my words;  
[Col. 1312C] let care for these teachings always occupy your mind.  
If you wish to be saved, always strive to imitate  
The life of the righteous, fleeing examples of the wicked.  
You will be joined to those whose deeds you follow.  
Choose the fellowship of saints, not of the reprobate.  

Oh, how rich are those for whom heavenly kingdoms are prepared!  
Thus are those exalted who are joined to the saints.  
Those who despise worldly joys will live joyfully;  
They know how to avoid the vices of wretched flesh.  
Their enemy lies conquered beneath their feet.  
To them it will truly be granted to possess the Lord without end,  
And the angelic choirs sounding forth divine praise,  
With whom before God they offer their trophy in praise.  

[Col. 1312D] If you keep with a chaste heart what I now tell you,  
You will again live joyfully without end, I am certain.  
But the wretched will weep, because they will see no joys.  
May no share ever be allotted to us with the reprobate:  
They will go to punishments and perish from you without end.  
The world is drawn to that party by the devil’s art.  
Those who cling to these defilements will suffer such losses.  

Therefore, moved by these counsels so often repeated,  
With discerning judgment beware of what will harm you.  
With unceasing care always meditate upon things to come:  
How fierce and strong will be death’s destruction;  
What way will open when the spirit departs;  
What it will do, or what companions it will have;  
How wretched hell is, and how noble the heavenly order;  
[Col. 1313A] what evils are for the condemned, what goods are gained by the blessed;  
How greatly those will rejoice whom supreme joys fill;  
Whom the holy vision of God and splendor of his face  
Will illumine and make forever glad.  

New joys will come to the mind seeking such things.  
With such devotion and spiritual sweetness  
Your mind will be nourished if it meditates on these continually.  
This practice makes minds pleasing to the Lord.  
It wholly drives out earthly cares, full of great anguish,  
And uproots the shoots of vices.  
Thus, touched by fear of eternal punishments, the mind  
Forsakes error and repels love of the world.  
Thereafter it burns with love for the highest goods.  
The wondrous gift of the Lord grants such good.  
For when an evil mind is changed, God accomplishes it.  

[Col. 1313B] God alone can bestow the gift of virtues;  
Thus he inwardly teaches the hearts of his servants  
Who pursue, speak, or meditate on good things.  
Thus the Lord raises to better habits those  
Whom he sees rising and seeking help.  

Therefore take care to submit yourself to Christ with pure faith;  
By his help you will flee the evils of this age.  
The courts of heaven stand open to the true believer.  
There you will always live, rich by God’s gift,  
If you sincerely wish to keep Christ’s commands.  
Those who follow his commands are joined to Christ.  
For eternal honor and the heavenly kingdom are given to them;  
The heavenly glory of paradise, due to the joyful,  
Will make them joyful, and eternal peace tranquil.  

You are already delighting in contemplating such things;  
[Col. 1313C] you gladly hear them and applaud these pious joys.  
Yet do not fail to know that they are attained more holily through great labors  
And are not found by chance.  

896 Yet although God freely grants these things to the blessed,  
No idle person bears the gifts of everlasting life  
Unless, made better, he has despised his own deeds.  
The Lord, who makes one worthy of these things, wishes him to be kind,  
Ready and fervent, but not a follower of these vanities.  

He does not advance toward the kingdom of heaven with a faithful mind,  
[Col. 1314A] being foolish and dull; but you ought rightly to believe  
Christ when he says: “The violent seize it.”  
That is, the austere, yet severe with discernment:  
Despising soft things and doing violence to the flesh,  
And always intent on obeying the Lord’s will.  

The matter is sufficiently well known and contains nothing new:  
The spirit perishes when the body seeks pleasures;  
And while the flesh is afflicted, the spirit is raised;  
But when the flesh is indulged, the spirit is mortally burdened.  
You yourself can see, by governing yourself, all that I show.  
With Scripture as guide, you will be able to know more.  
Sacred reading gives the mind seeking life a path.  

Receive these records of my writings concerning these matters.  
Do not regard with a heavy heart what I have shown you  
And gently instilled in you, but with a gracious mind.  
For whatever I have written will greatly profit you,  
[Col. 1314B] if the way of virtue and the path of salvation delight you.  

For the heavenly King, from whom nothing is hidden, is my witness:  
I have told you nothing except what I judged would profit you.  
Nor should the rule of truth seem harsh to you;  
For I have told the righteous to run by the narrow way.  
Thus the upright person ascends while always striving toward the heights.  
You will make this journey if you wish to ascend above.  

Perhaps I strive in vain to send this discourse to you, a boy,  
Because you do not grasp this meaning.  
But may the boundless Father give you mature understanding,  
Strengthen your age, and grant uprightness as well.  
May the Son of God himself, the hope of our offspring,  
The author of honor, the fount of enduring goodness,  
Give you the flowers of virtues and honorable habits.  

[Col. 1314C] May the Spirit of both, who touches the hearts of his own  
And becomes their teacher without the sound of words,  
Govern your mind and make it wise,  
Believing rightly and retaining good counsels,  
So that by living well and following holy commands  
You may deserve to possess the joy of true light—  
Light which knows no darkness and shines with surpassing beauty,  
And whoever receives it is blessed without end.  
May he who reigns Three and One grant you this gift.  

Amen.

## Rhythm on Contempt for the World (G)*

[Col. 1313]

[Col. 1313D]

O wondrous vanity! O lamentable  
Love of riches! O bitter poison!  
Why do you infect so many men, making precious  
What passes away more swiftly than a flame of tow?  

Wretched man, consider: death restrains all.  
Who has there been from the beginning who did not yield to death?  
No person knows when he will die;  
He who lives today perhaps decays tomorrow.  

I marvel that he who reflects on death rejoices,  
Since the human race is thus assigned to death  
And it is unknown whither a person passes after death.  
Therefore a certain wise man speaks thus of himself:  

[Col. 1314D]

When I think upon death, I grieve and weep:  
It is true that I shall die, but I do not know the time;  
I do not know my final end, to what choir I shall be joined.  
I pray to God that I may deserve to be joined with the saints.  

Why does the world serve beneath vain glory,  
Whose prosperity is transitory?  
Its power slips away as quickly  
As fragile potter’s vessels.  

Place more faith in letters written upon ice  
Than in the vain deceit of the wretched world:  
False in its rewards, in the semblance of virtue,  
It never possessed a time of trustworthiness.  

[Col. 1315A]

One should believe truthful men more  
Than the prosperities of the wretched world—  
More than false dreams and vanities,  
False pursuits and pleasures.  

897 Tell me: where is Solomon, once so noble?  
Or where is Samson, the unconquerable leader?  
Or handsome Absalom, wondrous in face?  
Or sweet Jonathan, greatly beloved?  

Whither has Caesar gone, lofty in empire?  
Or the splendid Rich Man, wholly given to feasting?  
Tell me: where is Tully, renowned in eloquence?  
Or Aristotle, greatest in intellect?  

So many illustrious nobles, so many past generations,  
So many faces of prelates, so many strong kingdoms,  
So many rulers of the world, such great power—  
[Col. 1315B] in the blink of an eye all are shut away.  

[Col. 1316A]

How brief a festival is this glory of the world!  
Its joys are like a human shadow;  
They always remove eternal rewards  
And lead people down hard byways.  

O food for worms! O mass of dust!  
O vanity of dew, why do you exalt yourself so?  
You wholly do not know whether you will live tomorrow.  
Do good to all while you can.  

This glory of the flesh, which is so highly valued,  
Is called in the sacred Scriptures a flower of hay.  
Like a light leaf snatched away by the wind,  
Thus human life is taken from the light.  

Call nothing yours that you can lose;  
What the world gives, it intends to take away.  
Think on things above; let your heart be in heaven.  
[Col. 1316B] Blessed is he who has been able to despise the world.

## The Same Bernard

[Col. 1315]

Tell me, man, why do you misuse  
The grace of discernment?  
Why do you abandon life’s way  
And make for punishments?  
You prefer ease to salvation  
And worthless things to precious ones.  
Neither fear of punishment bends you  
Nor hope of salvation draws you  
To seek the highest joys.  

Tell me, man, why do you misuse  
The grace of discernment?  

What is the worth of worldly glory—  
Look how you embrace it so!  
You see many signs  
That you are knowingly deceived.  
You follow the world that flees from you,  
And with that which slips away you slip,  
Following transient things.  
Thus you pass by enduring goods  
With a deaf ear.  

Tell me, man, why do you misuse  
The grace of discernment?  

Certainly you will not be excused  
By concealing such things.  
For if you evade them thus,  
Conscience remains afterward,  
Which does not keep hidden things silent;  
And you will not be able  
To avoid divine judgments.  
But if you are convicted,  
The sentence of death is manifest.  

Tell me, man, why do you misuse  
The grace of discernment?  

Do not trust in pardon  
If you repent too late.  
There is a decisive day;  
Unless you anticipate it  
With the fruit of worthy work  
And cleanse your guilt,  
[Col. 1315] misery will be yours  
Without mercy,  
Forever among the wretched.  

Tell me, man, why do you misuse  
The grace of discernment?  

Therefore see, when you come  
Into the Judge’s presence,  
Who will himself repay you  
According to your deeds:  
Let not your vices deprive you  
Of your glorious homeland.  
For if you oppose the world,  
You will be joined with the righteous  
In eternal joy.  

Tell me, man, why do you misuse  
The grace of discernment?  

O Christ’s patience  
And long waiting!  
O Christ’s wondrous goodness,  
O how great his compassion!  
O hardness of heart  
And haste toward death!  
Why do you delay? Why do you not consider,  
Man, how brief life is?  
Let meditation behold this:  
What we were at first.  

O vanity of vanities,  
Occupation with cares!  
O why is rank sought?  
Why the piling up of wealth?  
Whither does accumulation tend?  
Or what is greed worth?  
In the grave there is foulness,  
And outside, whitening.  
Let meditation behold this:  
What we were at first.  

O what bitterness of death!  
And how great the trembling  
When mortality now compels  
The separation to take place.  
What does pleasure profit?  
What festive delight?  
What do you now demand for life?  
O belated remembrance!  
Let meditation behold this:  
What we were at first.  

O bondage, what do you think of  
When you appear at judgment?  
O the enemy’s cruel rebuke  
And accusation!  
O pain and confusion!  
O terror, O darkness!  
O eternity of punishments  
And conflagration of fire!  
Let meditation behold this:  
What we were at first.  

O man, why do you not hasten  
That a dwelling may be given you  
Where there is happy immortality  
And no trembling,  
But everlasting exultation,  
The fellowship of saints,  
Abiding blessedness,  
And the joyful vision of God?  
Let meditation behold this:  
What we were at first.  

Since every person is hay  
And after hay becomes mire,  
Why, man, do you exalt yourself?  
See what you are and what you will be:  
Now you are a flower, and you will turn  
Into the ashes of a cinder.  

By the increase of years—  
Rather, by their diminishment—  
You are drawn toward non-being.  
Like a shadow, as it declines,  
Life rises and hastens;  
The finish of death closes it.  

[Col. 1317]

You are called *homo* from *humus*, “earth”;  
You quickly pass away, because you become  
Like smoke.  
You never remain in the same state  
While you are rolled beneath  
The turning of this life.  

O grievous lot! O harsh lot!  
O cruel law which nature  
[Col. 1317] proclaimed for the wretched!  
Man is born with sorrow,  
Lives with labor,  
And dies with fear.  

Therefore, if you know the condition  
Of your lot, why do you pursue  
The pleasure of the flesh?  
Remember that you will die  
[Col. 1318] and after death reap  
What you have sown here.  

You tread earth, bear earth,  
And will return to earth,  
You who are taken from earth.  
See what you are and what you will be:  
Now you are a flower, and you will turn  
Into the ashes of a cinder.

## Rhythmic Jubilation on the Name of Jesus

[Col. 1317]

898 Sweet remembrance of Jesus,  
Giving true joys to the heart;  
But sweeter than honey and all things  
Is his sweet presence.  

Nothing is sung more sweetly,  
Nothing heard more joyfully,  
Nothing thought more sweetly  
Than Jesus, God’s Son.  

Jesus, hope of the penitent,  
How merciful you are to those who ask!  
How good to those who seek you!  
But what are you to those who find you!  

Jesus, sweetness of hearts,  
Living fountain, light of minds,  
Exceeding every joy  
And every desire.  

Neither tongue can tell it  
Nor writing express it:  
One who has experienced it can believe  
What it is to love Jesus.  

I shall seek Jesus in my bed,  
In the closed chamber of my heart;  
In private and in public  
I shall seek him with diligent love.  

With Mary at dawn  
I shall seek Jesus in the tomb;  
With the plaintive cry of my heart  
I shall seek him with my mind, not my eyes.  

I shall bathe the tomb with tears,  
Filling the place with groans;  
I shall cast myself at Jesus’ feet,  
Clinging with close embraces.  

Jesus, wondrous king  
And noble conqueror,  
Ineffable sweetness,  
Wholly desirable.  

Remain with us, Lord,  
And enlighten us with your light,  
Driving away the mind’s darkness  
And filling the world with sweetness.  

When you visit our heart,  
Then truth shines within it,  
The world’s vanity becomes cheap,  
And charity burns within.  

[Col. 1317]

The love of Jesus, most sweet  
And truly most delightful,  
Is a thousand times more pleasing  
Than we are sufficient to tell.  

His Passion proves this,  
As does the shedding of his blood,  
Through which redemption  
And the vision of God are given us.  

All acknowledge Jesus;  
Seek his love.  
Seek Jesus ardently;  
In seeking, burn with love.  

Love one who loves thus;  
Return love for love.  
Run after this fragrance,  
And return vows for vows.  

Jesus, author of mercy,  
Hope of every joy,  
Fountain of sweetness and grace,  
The true delight of the heart.  

My good Jesus, may I feel  
The abundance of your love.  
Grant that through your presence  
I may see your glory.  

Though I am unable to speak worthily  
Of you, still let me not be silent:  
Love makes me dare,  
Since I rejoice only in you.  

Your love, Jesus,  
Is welcome refreshment of the mind,  
Filling it without weariness,  
899 while giving hunger to desire.  

Those who taste you hunger;  
Those who drink still thirst.  
They know no desire  
Except for the Jesus whom they love.  

He whom your love makes drunk  
Knows what savor Jesus has.  
How happy is he whom it satisfies!  
He has nothing more to desire.  

Jesus, angelic beauty,  
A sweet song in the ear,  
Wondrous honey in the mouth,  
Heavenly nectar in the heart.  

[Col. 1318]

I desire you a thousand times,  
My Jesus: when will you come?  
When will you make me glad?  
When will you satisfy me with yourself?  

Your continual love  
Is my unceasing languor;  
It is fruit sweet as honey  
And life everlasting to me.  

Jesus, highest kindness,  
Wondrous delight of the heart,  
Incomprehensible goodness—  
May your charity bind me.  

For me it is good to love  
Jesus and seek nothing more,  
To fail utterly to myself  
That I may be able to live for him.  

O my sweetest Jesus,  
Hope of the sighing soul,  
Devout tears seek you,  
The cry from my inmost mind seeks you.  

Wherever I may be,  
I desire Jesus with me.  
How glad I shall be when I find him!  
How happy when I hold him!  

Then embraces, then kisses  
That surpass draughts of honey;  
Then the blessed union with Christ—  
But in these there is a brief delay.  

Now I see what I sought;  
I hold what I desired.  
I languish with love of Jesus,  
And wholly burn in my heart.  

When Jesus is thus loved,  
This love is not extinguished;  
It does not grow cool or die,  
But increases and is kindled more.  

This love burns continually,  
Grows wonderfully sweet,  
Has delightful savor,  
And gives happiness and delight.  

This love, sent from heaven,  
Clings to me in my very marrow,  
Wholly kindles my mind;  
In this the spirit delights.  

[Col. 1319]

O blessed burning  
And ardent desire!  
O sweet refreshment—  
To love the Son of God!  

Jesus, flower of the virgin Mother,  
Love of our sweetness,  
To you be praise, honor of divinity,  
Kingdom of blessedness.  

Come, come, best King,  
Father of boundless glory;  
Shine more brightly upon the mind,  
You for whom we have so often waited.  

Jesus, clearer than the sun  
And sweeter than balm,  
Sweeter than every sweetness,  
More lovable than all others.  

Whose taste so moves us,  
Whose fragrance so refreshes us,  
In whom my mind fails—  
He alone suffices for one who loves.  

[Col. 1319]

You are the mind’s delight,  
Love’s consummation;  
You are my glory,  
Jesus, salvation of the world.  

My beloved, return,  
Companion at the Father’s right hand.  
You have successfully conquered the enemy;  
Now enjoy heaven’s kingdom.  

I shall follow you wherever you go;  
You cannot be taken away from me,  
Since you have taken away my heart,  
Jesus, praise of our race.  

Citizens of heaven, go out to meet him;  
Lift up your gates.  
Say to the conqueror:  
“Hail, illustrious King Jesus.”  

King of virtues, King of glory,  
King of splendid victory,  
Jesus, giver of pardon,  
Honor of the heavenly homeland.  

[Col. 1320]

You are the fountain of mercy,  
You are the light of the true homeland.  
Drive away the cloud of sorrow,  
Giving us the light of glory.  

The choir of heaven proclaims you  
And repeats your praises.  
Jesus gladdens the world  
And reconciles us to God.  

Jesus reigns in the peace  
That surpasses all understanding.  
My mind longs for this peace  
And hastens to enjoy it.  

Jesus has returned to the Father  
And entered the heavenly kingdom.  
My heart has departed from me;  
It has gone away with Jesus.  

Let us pursue him with praises,  
Vows, hymns, and prayers,  
That he may grant us to enjoy  
The heavenly dwellings with him. Amen.

## Rhythmic Prayer to Each Several Member of Christ Suffering and Hanging on the Cross (G)

[Col. 1319]

900 To the Feet.

Hail, salvation of the world;  
Hail, hail, dear Jesus.  
I would truly wish to attach myself  
To your cross—you know why.  
Grant me the possession of yourself.  

As though you were present, I draw near;  
Indeed, I believe you present.  
Oh, how pure I behold you here!  
See, I cast myself down before you;  
Be ready to pardon.  

The nails in your feet, the hard wounds,  
And the marks so grievously impressed,  
I clasp with affection,  
Trembling at the sight of you  
And mindful of your wounds.  

Let us, wounded people, give thanks  
For such great love.  
O lover of sinners,  
Restorer of the broken—  
O sweet father of the poor!  

Whatever in me is broken,  
Scattered, or torn apart,  
Sweet Jesus, heal it all;  
Restore it; make it whole  
With so merciful a medicine.  

I seek you upon your cross  
With a pure heart, as best I can.  
There, I hope, you will heal me:  
Heal me, and I shall be whole,  
Washing in your blood.

[Col. 1319] Make your ruddy wounds

And your wounds so deeply pierced

Be inscribed upon my heart,

That I may be wholly fastened to you,

Loving you in every way.

Sweet Jesus, gracious God,

To you I cry, though guilty:

Show yourself kindly toward me,

Lest you drive me, unworthy as I am,

From your holy feet,

As I fall prostrate before the cross

And embrace those feet.

Good Jesus, do not despise me,

But look down from the holy cross

With the grace of compassion.

Standing upright upon this cross,

See me, O my beloved;

Turn me wholly toward yourself.

“Be whole,” say openly:

“I forgive you everything.”

### To the Knees

Hail, Jesus, king of saints,

The hoped-for expectation of sinners,

Hanging like a criminal on the wood of the cross,

True God made man,

With failing knees bent.

O how poor! O how naked!

What a spectacle you have become upon the cross,

Wholly made the mockery

Of those who deride you—

Yet willingly, not under compulsion—

Bruised in every limb!

[Col. 1320] Your blood, poured out abundantly,

Flows without ceasing;

Wholly bathed in gore,

You stand in the utmost pain,

Girded with a worthless cloth.

O infinite Majesty!

O unheard-of poverty!

Who, in return for such great love,

Seeks you in truth,

Giving blood for blood?

What answer shall I make to you,

Vile in deed and hard in heart?

What shall I repay to the lover

Who chose to die for me,

Lest I should die a double death?

Your love is a mighty love,

Which the laws of death do not overcome.

O how tenderly, in my distress,

You cherish me beneath your care,

Lest I be wounded by death’s bite!

Behold, because of love for you,

I embrace you with shame.

Fit me closely to yourself;

You plainly know the reason,

But bear with it and overlook it.

May what I do not burden you,

But heal and cleanse me,

Defiled and sick as I am,

By the blood flowing here all over you,

So that no stain remains.

As you stand bloodied upon this cross,

Despised and stretched out,

[Col. 1321] Impel me to seek you,

And fulfill this desire of mine,

For I shall do what I long for.

Let this be my first care:

to seek you with a pure mind.

It is no labor, nor shall I be burdened;

Rather, I shall be healed and cleansed

When I have embraced you.

### To the Hands

Hail, Jesus, good shepherd,

Wearied in the struggle,

Who have been stretched out upon the wood

And fastened to the wood,

With your holy hands spread wide.

Holy hands, hail to you,

Filled with fresh roses,

Harshly joined to these branches

And pierced by cruel iron,

901 With so many drops running down.

Behold, your blood flows everywhere,

Abundantly, from each hand,

Red as a rose,

The price of great salvation.

Your hands pierced by nails

And made purple with blood—

First with my heart because of love,

Then drinking with a thirsty mouth,

I drink the dripping blood.

O how freely you expose yourself,

Ready for the wicked and the good alike!

You draw the sluggish, call the devout,

And receive them into your arms,

Prepared freely for all.

Behold, I present myself to you,

Wounded and bloodied.

You always pity the sick;

Therefore do not be burdened by me,

For you are present to those who love you.

Thus stretched upon this cross,

Draw my senses into yourself;

Make my power, will, and understanding

Serve your cross;

Fit me to your arms.

In such broad charity,

Draw me in truth;

For the sake of your life-giving cross,

Draw me to the palm of the cross,

Bringing an end to my vices.

Holy hands, I embrace you

And, groaning, delight in you.

I give thanks for such great wounds,

Hard nails, and holy drops,

Giving tears with kisses.

Washed in your blood,

I wholly commend myself to you.

May these your holy hands

Defend me, Jesus Christ,

In my final perils.

[Col. 1321] ### To the Side

Hail, Jesus, supremely good,

Exceedingly inclined to spare:

How bitterly your emaciated limbs

Have been stretched

Upon the burning branch of the cross!

Hail, side of the Savior,

Where the honey of sweetness lies hidden,

Where the power of love is displayed,

Whence springs the fountain of blood

That washes defiled hearts.

Behold, I draw near to you.

Spare me, Jesus, if I offend.

Though with a modest countenance,

Yet of my own will I come to you

To search your wounds.

Hail, gentle opening,

From which a pure vein flows:

An open and deep gate,

Redder than a rose,

A saving remedy.

Your fragrance is above wine,

Driving away the serpent’s poison;

Your drink is the drink of life.

You who thirst, come here;

Open, sweet wound.

Red wound, open;

Make my heart feel you.

Allow me to pass into you;

I would enter wholly.

Open to the poor man who knocks.

With my mouth I touch you

And ardently press you to myself.

I dip my heart into you

And, with burning heart, lick you;

Draw my whole self into you.

O how sweet is this taste!

Whoever tastes you, Jesus Christ,

Conquered by your sweetness,

Could die for love,

Loving you alone, uniquely.

Hide me in this hollow;

Bring my heart deep within,

That, hidden there, it may grow warm

And rest in peace,

And fear no one at all.

At the hour of death, may my breath

Enter your side, Jesus;

May it expire hence and go into you,

Lest the cruel lion attack it,

But may it remain with you.

### To the Breast

Hail, God, my salvation,

Sweet Jesus, my love.

Hail, venerable breast,

To be touched with trembling,

The dwelling-place of love.

Hail, throne of the Trinity,

Ark of broad charity,

[Col. 1322] Support of the weak,

Peace and rest of the weary,

Dining-room of the humble.

Hail, venerable Jesus,

Ever worthy to be sought.

Attend to me here, as I am present;

Set me aflame as I draw near,

With inward grace.

Grant me a breast that is pure,

Burning, devout, and groaning;

A will self-denying,

Ever conformed to you,

Joined to an abundance of virtues.

Sweet Jesus, gracious shepherd,

Son of God and Mary,

From the abundant fountain of your heart,

Kind Father, wash away

The foulness of my defilement.

Hail, splendor and image

Of the begetting of the highest God;

From your full treasures

Flow mercifully as a gift

To the desolate and needy.

Sweet breast of Jesus Christ,

By your gift may I be made upright,

Freed from sins,

Burning with the fire of charity,

That I may ever remember you.

You are the abyss of wisdom;

The harmony of angels

Praises you together. From you flowed

That which John, reclining, drank:

Make me dwell in you.

Hail, fountain of kindness,

The fullness of deity

Dwells bodily in you.

May the counsel you bestow

Heal the vanity within me.

Hail, true temple of God;

I pray, have mercy on me.

You, ark of every good,

Place me among the elect,

O rich vessel, God of all.

### To the Heart

Heart of the highest King, hail!

I greet you with a joyful heart.

I delight to embrace you,

And this heart of mine longs

To speak to you, that you may give it life.

By what love were you overcome?

By what pain were you tormented,

When you poured yourself out wholly

902 That you might impart yourself to us

And raise us from death?

O death, how bitter,

How cruel, how greedy you were!

You entered the chamber

In which the life of the world lives,

Biting you, sweetest heart!

[Col. 1323] Because of the death you endured

When you failed for me,

Beloved heart of my heart,

Bear my affection into yourself:

This is what I desire most.

O sweet and dearly beloved heart,

Cleanse my heart, entangled

And hardened in vain things.

Make it devout and fearful,

Driving away dreadful coldness.

Through the marrow of my heart,

A sinner and guilty man,

May your love be conveyed,

By which my whole heart may be carried away,

Languishing from the wound of love.

Expand and open yourself,

Like a rose wondrously fragrant.

Join yourself to my heart;

Anoint it and pierce it.

What does one who loves you suffer?

What he does, indeed, he does not know,

Nor can he restrain himself;

He grants no measure to love.

He would wish to die many deaths,

Whoever is overcome by love.

With the living voice of my heart I cry:

Sweet heart, for I love you.

Bend down to my heart,

That it may be able to join itself to you

With a breast devoted to you.

May it live in your love

And not sleep in numbness.

May it pray to you, weep to you,

Adore you, honor you,

Enjoying you at every moment.

Rose of the heart, open,

[Col. 1323] Whose fragrance wonderfully breathes forth;

Deign to expand yourself;

Make my heart pant

With the flame of longing.

Grant heart to be joined with heart,

To be wounded with you, Jesus.

For heart is likened to heart

If my heart is pierced

By arrows of reproach.

Bring your heart into my bosom,

That my heart may be close to you,

In sorrow that is joyful,

With the deformed Beautiful One,

So that it can scarcely contain itself.

May it rest here, may it remain here;

Behold, it is now moved after you

And ardently wishes to thirst for you.

Jesus, do not oppose it,

That it may think well of you.

### To the Face

Hail, bloodied head,

Wholly crowned with thorns,

Battered, wounded,

Struck with a reed,

Your face smeared with spittle.

Hail, you whose sweet countenance,

Changed and neglected,

Changed its bloom,

Wholly turned to pallor—

Whom [Note: [Col. 1323B] Add “the court of heaven desires,” or something similar.] the court of heaven desires.

All vigor and freshness

Have departed from it; nor do I wonder.

Death appears in your countenance,

As you hang wholly in exhaustion,

Worn away by sickly emaciation.

[Col. 1324] Thus afflicted, thus despised,

Thus slain for me,

Show yourself with a bright countenance

To so unworthy a sinner,

Bearing the sign of love.

In this your Passion,

Acknowledge me, good Shepherd,

I who have taken honey from your mouth,

A draught of milk with sweetness,

Above every delight.

Do not reject me as guilty,

Nor disdain me as unworthy.

Now that your death is near,

Incline your head here

To rest in my arms.

I would rejoice to join myself

To your holy Passion,

To die with you upon this cross.

Grant that I, a lover of the cross,

May die beneath your cross.

For your death, so bitter,

I give thanks, dear Jesus.

You who are merciful, gracious God,

Grant what your guilty servant asks:

that I may not end apart from you.

Since I must die,

Do not then be absent from me.

In the fearful hour of death,

Come, Jesus, without delay;

Protect and deliver me.

When you command me to depart,

Dear Jesus, then appear.

O lover to be embraced,

Then show yourself

Upon the saving cross.

[Col. 1323]

## Devout Prayer (G)

### To the Lord Jesus and Blessed Mary His Mother

[Col. 1323A] 903 You, the only Son of the supreme Father,

Maker of the world and ruler of its fabric,

Look upon afflicted sinners

With the regard of divine mercy,

Gracious Father.

You, Mother of the supreme Son,

Holding the key of our help,

Nourish with the milk of your counsel

The pilgrims of this exile,

Gracious Mother.

May those who breathe again in your name

Be comforted, O good Lord—

You who, to take away the world’s crime,

Deigned to be born of a virgin,

Father of your Mother.

[Col. 1323B] May those thirsting for your consolations

Be comforted, O good Lady.

[Col. 1324A] From you alone, blessed woman,

These two names are proclaimed:

Virgin Mother.

O image of the Father’s substance!

You are the splendor of the Father’s glory;

You are the true light of righteousness,

From whom flows the fullness

Of all grace.

O queen of David’s kingdom!

You are the rod of the Lord’s flower;

You are the ark of angelic bread,

By which our solitude deserves

To be refreshed.

Power and wisdom of the Father,

Sweetly ordering all things,

[Col. 1324B] You and the Father are one substance:

Equal honor and the same glory

[Col. 1325A] Belong to both.

Star of the sea, queen of the age,

You are the Mother of that little one

Whom faithful peoples adore,

All always and each one always,

And everywhere.

O wondrous Holy One of saints,

Desirable to the whole world,

Mighty man and humble God:

None is, nor shall be, like you,

My God.

O sweetest holy one of holy women,

Alone most worthy of so great a childbirth,

So that from your most pure flesh

The highest majesty might be born,

[Col. 1325B] God and man.

Jesus Christ, unfailing fountain,

Fountain refreshing human hearts,

I sigh for you; thirsting for you alone.

You alone will be sufficient for me,

Son of God.

Mother of Christ, virgin glory,

Seated upon the heavenly throne,

Your name, honey-sweet in savor,

Melts the iron-like affection

Of my heart.

Highest good, full of sweetness,

True light from true light,

At the hearing of whose name alone

The heart of the righteous is filled

With wondrous richness.

[Col. 1325C] Resting-place of the highest good,

Sweet cellar of sweet wine,

Which the King of heaven,

The sweetness that makes sweet things sweet,

Chose beforehand as his own.

Father of fathers, exalted above others,

Restorer of the human race:

O you who for us took flesh

From the flesh of a poor woman,

You assumed flesh.

Mother of mothers and Virgin of virgins,

Storehouse of humankind’s salvation,

O you who, from pure flesh, conceived the Lord

Without the mingling

[Col. 1325D] Of fleshly seed.

Hear, I pray, you who grant grace,

The misery of this sinner;

And through your mercy

Grant me forgiveness

For my sins.

Hear, I pray, O full of grace,

The sighs of this sinner,

And by your mercy

Reconcile me to my God,

Good Mother.

Make acceptable to yourself, Father,

The groaning of this sinner.

[Col. 1326A] Cancel the debt of my guilt,

For I show forth evil deserving,

And have shown it forth.

Make acceptable to yourself, Mother,

This tearful voice of the sinner.

Render God merciful to me,

Lest he prove inexorable,

Whom I have offended.

O child of an untouched mother,

Hear the lament of a wretched soul,

Which, lying in the dust of sin,

Laments that it rots away

Like a beast of burden.

O untouched Virgin who has borne a child,

To you my wretched mind cries,

[Col. 1326B] Which from tenderest age until now

Has always run unrestrained

To unspeakable crimes.

Gracious Father, correct one who has gone astray;

Stretch out your gracious hand to one who falls.

Now raise me from the mire of filth,

And direct me into the way

Of your commandments.

Gracious Mother, visit one who prays;

Remember me with a merciful heart.

Cry out before kindly Jesus,

That he may remit the debts

Of my sins.

Be gracious to us, Father,

Whose brother and companion you are.

[Col. 1326C] We praise you, bless you,

Adore and love you

With our whole mind.

Be gracious to us, Mother,

Whose sister and companion you are.

Make our hearts willing

And devoted to proclaim

Your praises.

Blessed Creator of all,

Bless the minds of the faithful

Who bless your name,

Whom you saved by the benefit

Of your death.

Blessed are you among women;

Bless those who bless you,

[Col. 1326D] By your blessed breasts,

He who gives food to the hungry,

Whom you nursed.

Praise and honor be to the Son of God,

Salvation, strength, and blessing.

Blessed be his incarnation,

His death and resurrection,

For ever.

Blessed be the Father of lights;

Blessed be the Virgin of virgins.

May my heart bless the Lord

And thirst for the everlasting fountain

Of sweetness. Amen.

## Prose for the Nativity of the Lord

[Col. 1327]

[Col. 1327] Let the faithful choir,

Rejoicing,

Exult:

Alleluia.

The bed of the untouched Virgin

Has brought forth

The King of kings:

A wondrous thing.

The Angel of Counsel

Was born of the Virgin,

The sun from a star.

The sun that knows no setting,

The star ever gleaming,

Ever bright.

As a star produces a ray,

So the Virgin brings forth her Son

In like manner.

Neither is the star corrupted by its ray,

Nor the Mother by her Son.

The lofty cedar of Lebanon

Is made like hyssop

In our valley.

The Word, being of the Most High,

Endured to be embodied,

Having taken flesh.

Isaiah sang it;

The Synagogue remembers it,

Yet never ceases

To be blind.

[Col. 1328] If it does not believe its own prophets,

Let it believe even the Gentiles:

These things were foretold

In Sibylline verses.

Unhappy one, hasten;

Believe at least the things of old.

Why will you be condemned,

Wretched people?

Consider him whom Scripture teaches:

Behold, the woman who has borne him

Has given birth to him.

Amen.

## Ancient Rhythms on Monastic Life

(Fabricius, *Bibliotheca mediae et infimae latinitatis*, at the end of volume III.—In certain manuscripts attributed to Bernard.) (G)

[Col. 1327] 904 2. If you wish to be a monk in community,

Live the life of this way of life,

That you may be so in reality as well as in name.

Cleanse the filth of your mind,

That God may be a joyful praise

In both the inner and outward person.

Let God alone be loved,

To whom alone should be left

All praise and glory.

Honor, power, and might

Be to him whose majesty

Fills and rules all things.

It is not yours, O man, to wish

To be honored or praised,

Since you belong to a wretched life.

Whatever honor you gain here,

Unless you devote it wholly to the Lord,

You lose your life.

Clerics would not so easily seek honors

If they also felt the labors.

He who wishes to preside, not to benefit,

Loses his very being,

Worthy of a double punishment.

They are ready for honors,

Ungrateful for labors,

Young men now together with old.

Everything is given to rank,

Little or nothing to holiness,

In these times of ours.

Thus the life of laypeople

Differs little from the habits

Of swine.

[Col. 1327] They feast beyond measure;

Within and without they are blinded,

Full of evil habits.

There is rare talk of the salvation of souls,

But the extent of lands

Is sought.

He who can become richer,

Or be raised higher,

Is called blessed.

The world now threatens its end,

Defiled as it is by so many evils,

As Truth foretold:

Charity now grows cold,

Every holy person falls silent,

And impiety abounds.

The powerful man laughs at the powerless,

The crafty man at the innocent,

The young man at the old.

A man is supplanted by his equal,

A child opposes his father,

The rich man despises the poor.

A man is thought holy today

Who is now less defiled

By evils and crimes.

If you seek a model of life,

Do not now seek it in people,

But in books.

The law has perished from the priest,

All virtues are perishing,

Counsel from the old man.

We have many teachers,

But very few doers

In mortal life.

[Col. 1328] If I had here an abiding city

In this captivity of life,

I would weep.

This would plainly be a city

In which truth was unknown,

If I were to live here forever.

Alas, alas! Why is man created,

When he is defiled with so many evils?

Whether he wills it or not, he dies.

The unhappy man is compelled

To avoid what is good

Or to love what is evil.

Hence no one should now wonder

If every righteous person refuses

To be consoled here.

Indeed, he is sufficiently to be lamented

And rejected by God

Who does not reject the world.

The truly holy person is comforted

And made blessed in this alone:

that the world shall pass away.

Weep over this downfall of the world,

And over your sins, O unclean ones,

Whose sorrow will come.

Return therefore to yourself,

O man, who have miserably fallen away from yourself;

Consider why you were made.

God made you like himself,

But you make yourself unlike him,

Increasing your crimes.

Once companion of angels,

You keep the law of beasts,

Having become like them.

[Col. 1329] Food is for the belly, and the belly for food;

You do not know how to restrain these and it,

And therefore you are frail.

Rise, wretched one, who sleep;

Imitate the monks

Of ancient times.

Holding to the way of life,

They willingly despised

Wealth and bodily strength.

They were crucified to the world

With its vices, and pierced through

By the sword of charity.

They regarded this life as of little value,

For they clung to heaven

With great longing.

They severely disciplined the body,

Devoted themselves to reading,

And prayed continually.

They were never idle,

Affectionate toward all.

Go, do likewise.

Keep yourself devout;

Flee all that you see;

Choose poverty.

Do not let a place of lowliness

Or of remoteness distress you,

But love to be unknown.

You shall subject yourself to a superior;

Whatever he commands, you shall observe,

And that willingly.

Do not judge the deeds of superiors,

But you ought to avoid

The gall of envy.

Reprove yourself;

Take diligent care

Never to judge anyone.

[Col. 1329] Giving an account for yourself,

Before you utter a word,

That you may vindicate yourself.

It will be salutary for you

If you strive to love and to be loved

By every person.

Whatever you do is rejected by God

And not praised

Unless you preserve peace.

Let young people be loved,

Let elders be revered;

Be dear to all.

Do not show partiality,

But love the good life

In every person.

It is good, as Paul says,

To rejoice with those who rejoice

And to weep with those who weep.

Though ordered, you shall be patient

With your disordered

Brothers.

Bear patiently

The infirmities of their bodies

And likewise the poverty of their habits.

Do not wish to appear great,

Nor to receive praise

In this wretched life.

Beware of being singular;

But whatever you do,

Do it in common.

Sing, chant psalms, read, pray,

As all do; labor,

Live, and do not do otherwise.

Be first at work,

But slow to anger,

[Col. 1330] And the last to wrath.

Be subject to all;

Never say anything other

Than what is in your mind.

Fill every hour

With hymns and psalms, and love

To preserve silence.

Beyond this, love prayer

And reading,

The nourishment of cloistered persons.

Having clothing and food,

As the Apostle says,

Seek nothing more.

Do not complain about color;

If it is cheap, then rejoice,

And so you will be sober.

Beware of curiosity in clothing

Or greediness for varied foods.

Thus you will not be sleepy,

Nor drunken with drink,

Nor occupied with idle talk.

It is exceedingly dangerous

For a cloistered person to be talkative,

When he ought to be silent.

Jokes may indeed be endured,

But never repeated—

Jokes that it would be shameful

To utter.

Flee every sin

If you wish to see at peace

The Savior of all.

Pray to him with heart and mouth,

That on the day and at the hour of death

He may be your help.

Amen.
